plan: Store the workspace as a deep-copied dict tree; sections/groups are the only container kinds and hold child items in list order.
Implement one recursive depth-first generator (_walk) and drive total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline off it so every operation is uniform across nesting levels.

For notes, strip [[?identifier]] tokens before counting \b\w+\b words; references contribute their declared word_count; markers come from note text plus reference unresolved lists, deduplicated and sorted.
Render the outline deterministically: workspace title, then '  ' * depth + 'kind: title' per item in list order, depth starting at 1 for top-level items.

Make move atomic by validating everything first (string ids, both ids resolvable, destination is workspace/section/group, index in 0..len, destination not the item or any descendant) and only then popping the node from its parent list and inserting it, so failed moves never touch state.
to_data returns copy.deepcopy of the internal tree.
mechanisms: uniform depth-first traversal shared by all queries
recursive aggregation of word counts with kind-specific contributions
deterministic pre-order outline rendering with depth-based indentation
containment/no-cycle validation (destination must be a container and not the moved item or its descendant)
validate-then-mutate atomic move leaving state unchanged on any error
